headToHead.voiceVerdict: Much closer than round 1, still the bar. Prince now owns two shapes nobody else in the cast uses: the P.S. turn (gracious body, the real point after the full stop: the harpist, Mother insists it was accurate, your mother has been knighted) and the email header (Subject:/Re:/Auto-reply:). Cover the names on those and you still know him. But roughly a quarter of the bank speaks in a generic royal-decree register ('I shall have it translated.', 'Pity. The banns have been read. I shall have them unread.', 'Charming. My father exiled a man for less.', 'Year one of our reign... I will ignore them graciously.') that is the house shape of Maximilian, a star on this same show ('How brave.' 'I shall have that removed.'), and of Sir Quill ('I shall have it set to harpsichord by morning'). With names covered those lines are a coin flip between three characters. Vera has no lookalike: her complaint-as-boast (#45) and tag-question complicity (#47) belong to her alone.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Tie. Ours is tighter than the bar: almost every line under 17 words, turn on the last beat, and the fee crutch is gone (five fee/charge endings in 112 lines). 'Small letters. Very high up.' and 'The harpist outside your door is unrelated.' are better built than most Vera lines. Against that, about a dozen lines close on a two-word deadpan tag that comments on the joke instead of landing it ('Frankly, suspicious.', 'Honestly, fair.', 'Purely decorative.', 'Purely ceremonial.', 'It exists.', 'It seemed polite.', 'The mint is thrilled.', 'Literally.' twice in the same question slot), and several jokes are the same mechanism run five to eight times, so the second time the viewer sees it coming. Vera's lines are looser but no two of hers turn the same way.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar, narrowly. 'Exactly the kind of person who opens attachments', 'kindly lower your font size', 'Small letters. Very high up.' and 'I have bought the station. You work for us now.' would all clip. Vera's clip lines have appetite and stakes aimed at the listener (murder, poison, losers like you) and fans quote them as catchphrases; Prince's presumption mostly lands on one stake, whether the star said yes, and the 419 frame is old enough that the audience arrives ahead of the openers.
headToHead.overall: If both ran tonight Vera is still the better written character, but by less than in round 1. Prince now has a posture (calm presumption) and two signature shapes (P.S., email header). What keeps him behind is that his presumption is spent on one object, consent to the marriage, and that his royal register leaks into Maximilian's and Quill's.

Real-person allusion, unnamed: "Darling, my grandmother is on the money. Literally. Pick a note." points at a real monarch on real banknotes. Low risk, but it is the only line that leans on a real family.

Too soft for a wingman twist whose brief is sabotage: "Crumb is warm and very honest. Ask Crumb what it thinks of you. Then come and find me." and "Vex has already chosen your ideal partner. It is me. She is furious about it." barely touch the rival.

biggestGap: Prince's presumption is spent on one object, whether the star said yes: a smile, a cringe, a no, an opened envelope and a morning acceptance are all converted into consent in eight lines, which makes the spine one joke on repeat and pushes it toward no-means-yes. In the next pass treat the engagement as old news never argued for, and aim the presumption at everything around it the way Vera presumes you will cover her murder: the star already has palace duties, a seat on the privy council and opinions on the swans; the rivals are already on staff or in exile; and say it in his email shapes (P.S., Subject:, cc, signature block) instead of 'I shall have it [verb]ed', which belongs to Maximilian.
